applicable_when: The kernel is severely register-bound: 168 registers/thread with block_size=128 limits the SM to only 3 blocks (18.75% theoretical occupancy), and achieved occupancy collapses further to 6.25% due to workload imbalance across 123 blocks on 132 SMs (< 1 full wave). The fixed BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32 tile configuration is the root cause. Additionally, the B matrix is loaded with stride 192*idx_n (column-major access into a row-major buffer), causing 7.9-way shared memory bank conflicts that stall warps for 45% of cycles. Reducing tile sizes via autotuning will cut register pressure, raise occupancy, and cover all 132 SMs. Using block_ptr for B loads enables TMA on Hopper and eliminates bank conflicts.
